summary: Wotje Airport (WTE) is a small regional airstrip serving Wotje Atoll, a coral atoll in the Ratak Chain of the Marshall Islands in the central Pacific Ocean. The atoll has historical significance as a former Japanese military and seaplane base during World War II, and remnants of wartime infrastructure can still be found across the island. Today it functions primarily as a domestic link connecting remote atoll communities to Majuro and other islands in the chain.
faqs:
Q: Which airline operates flights to Wotje Airport?
A: Air Marshall Islands provides scheduled inter-island service to Wotje, typically using small twin-engine aircraft suited to the short runway.

Q: How long is the runway at Wotje Airport?
A: The airport features a single short paved runway suitable primarily for small turboprop aircraft used on domestic routes.

Q: Are there customs or immigration facilities at Wotje?
A: No, Wotje is a domestic airport only. All international travelers must clear customs and immigration in Majuro before continuing on to Wotje.

Q: When is the best time to fly to Wotje?
A: Flights operate year-round, but calm weather and clearer seas make the dry season (December to April) generally the most pleasant time to visit.
transport_tips: Getting to Wotje typically requires a connecting flight from Majuro International Airport, as there are no international flights into Wotje. Ground transport on the atoll is informal; travelers usually arrange rides in advance with a local contact or guesthouse. A small boat is needed to reach the airstrip from the main islet, and schedules are infrequent.
local_tip: Bring small cash denominations and extra snacks or supplies, as shops on Wotje have limited inventory and may not stock what you need during your stay.
